The type errors are pre-existing (pi allows `.ts` import extensions at runtime; `pageup`/`pagedown` KeyId issues were there before my changes). My edits introduce no new errors.

## Summary

The crash was caused by the **help line** (line 74 in the render output) being 84 columns wide in a 76-column terminal — it was rendered without any width truncation:

```
 ⏎ send · ctrl+p model · ctrl+t deep-research · ctrl+r recap · ↑↓ scroll · esc close
```

### Fix in `extensions/perplexity/research-panel.ts`

1. **Imported `truncateToWidth`** from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`.
2. **Wrapped the help line** in `truncateToWidth(..., innerWidth)` — the direct cause of the crash.
3. Also defensively truncated the other hand-built single-line strings that weren't using `wrapTextWithAnsi`/`Markdown.render`:
   - the **header line** (previously only padded with spaces, could overflow if status message grew),
   - the **divider line** (border + scroll indicator),
   - the **input line** (`▸ ` + rendered input),
   - **citation source lines** (`[i] title url`) in `renderAnswer`, which were never wrapped and could easily exceed width on long URLs/titles.

The transcript body itself (`renderQuery`/`renderAnswer`) already uses `wrapTextWithAnsi` and `Markdown.render(width)`, so those are fine. The panel should now render safely at any terminal width.
I find the UX a bit fiddly, I used the arrow to navigate the thread but it makes it very slow, can we simplify it to make it look like @extensions/review.ts ?

## Summary

I rewrote `extensions/perplexity/research-panel.ts` to fix the fiddly UX. Two root problems:

### 1. Slowness (the real culprit)
Every `render()` call ran `new Markdown(...).render(width)` for **every transcript turn**, and `handleInput` triggered a re-render on **every keystroke and every arrow press**. So scrolling the thread re-rendered all the markdown each frame — that's why arrows felt "very slow."

**Fix:** Added a rendered-transcript cache keyed by `(content version, width)`. The full flat line array is only recomputed when the transcript content actually changes (new turn, streaming delta, status change) or the terminal is resized. Scrolling now just slices the cached array — instant. Typing in the input no longer re-runs the Markdown renderer either.

### 2. Layout & keys simplified to match review.ts
Restructured `render()` into the bordered, composable style used by `extensions/review.ts`:
- **Top border** carries the bold accent title + model + status (like review.ts's `DynamicBorder` + title).
- **Transcript body** — auto-tails while streaming; `↑/↓` scroll instantly and re-engage auto-tail once you reach the bottom.
- **Bottom border** with a scroll indicator (`start-end/total`).
- **Input line** + **dim help line**, both width-truncated (this also keeps the earlier crash fix).

### Key handling simplified
- Dropped `PageUp`/`PageDown` (they were the source of the pre-existing `KeyId` type errors and added clutter).
- Removed `Enter`/`onSubmit` manual routing — `Input` already handles printable keys; Enter submission flows through `input.onSubmit`.
- `Ctrl+P` cycle model, `Ctrl+T` deep-research, `Ctrl+R` recap, `Esc` cancel/close — unchanged.

The `ResearchPanel` constructor signature, `prefill()`, and the `TranscriptTurn`/`ResearchResult`/`ResearchPanelDeps` types are identical, so `index.ts` needs no changes.

## Topic
Application development on the reMarkable tablet, including the official SDK workflow and a specific Rust-based custom app example (`riddle`).

## Key Findings
- The reMarkable official SDK provides a cross-compiler toolchain, shared libraries, and header files for building software on a host machine and deploying it to the tablet; the SDK is product-specific and Developer Mode may need to be enabled (which can erase device content on some models, so backup first). [1]
- The official development path centers on building **Qt Quick / QML** applications using the SDK, with a workflow of: enable Developer Mode, install the matching SDK, source the SDK environment, build locally with the cross-compiler, then copy the executable to the device over SSH. [1]
- The `riddle` project (a Tom Riddle diary app for the reMarkable Paper Pro) is built as a **Rust application** using CMake-based cross-compilation, integrated with reMarkable's Qt-based UI stack and system libraries via the vendor toolchain. [2]
- `riddle` supports two build targets: a **host build** using standard Rust toolchain (`cargo run`) for local development/testing, and a **device build** using the reMarkable Paper Pro SDK (Yocto-based) with CMake orchestrating cross-compilation via a toolchain file that configures the correct compiler, sysroot, and linker settings. [2]
- Community tools and launchers exist as an alternative to official app development, providing custom interfaces and extended functionality beyond the stock app model. [1]

## Sources
[1] SDK documentation — reMarkable Developer Portal — https://developer.remarkable.com/documentation/sdk
[2] The diary of Tom Riddle for the reMarkable Paper Pro — GitHub — https://github.com/MaximeRivest/riddle

- Which reMarkable model is being targeted, and does Developer Mode need to be enabled on it?
